title: Far-Fetched

inlines.v: F'AR-FETCHED, adjective 1. Brought from a remote place. Whose pains have earned the far-fetched spoil. 2. Studiously sought; not easily or naturally deduced or introduced; forced; strained. York with all his far-fetched policy. So we say, far-fetched arguments; far-fetched rhymes; far-fetched analogy. [Far-fet, the same, is not used.]
